title: expiring-cert-promoter: staged cert pre-provisioning, HSM-aware KMS labels, and Helm/Terraform hooks for safe rollback
author: Clara Mendes
description:
Motivation: Private installs running in regulated environments require predictable certificate and key promotion procedures that tolerate HSM-backed KMS constraints and support fast, safe rollback. This PR introduces a small controller (expiring-cert-promoter) plus Helm/Terraform integration to pre-provision replacement TLS certs and KMS key labels, stage rolling rekey operations, and expose explicit rollout/rollback hooks to the installer. The goal is zero-downtime certificate replacement with an audited handoff and automatic safe fallback when HSM bindings or Vault sync lag.

What this changes: adds a new operator that monitors cert expiry windows and pre-stages a candidate certificate + key-wrapping metadata (labels/annotations) into Vault/SealedSecrets; introduces a KMS-labeling extension in the Terraform KMS module to declare promoted keys and HSM-operator compatible labels; updates the private-installer Helm chart with pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks that perform dry-run promotion and a staged traffic drain; includes a rollback-safe reencrypt plan that reverts pointers without destroying promoted keys for a grace period.

Key constraints considered: HSM-backed keys cannot be rewrapped in-place on some vendors (requires create-new + promote). Vault replication latency across zones can be multi-second; hooks include idempotent reconciliation and an explicit 'promote-confirm' gate. The controller keeps promotion metadata in annotations to allow operators to inspect staged candidates and abort promotions before final cutover.

Security notes: promotion operations mark promoted keys with a revocation-delay tag and write an audit entry to the installer audit log; we avoid exposing raw private key material outside Vault/HSM. The chart changes add RBAC rules scoped to the promoter service account and document least-privilege IAM bindings for the Terraform module.

This description contains implementation details, upgrade guidance, and manual rollback steps to help SRE and platform teams run the promotion in low-trust environments.

review_comments: Samir Patel: Nice direction — can you clarify the failure mode if Vault replication lags >30s? Is there a cleanup path for half-promoted keys?

Clara Mendes: Answered: the controller marks candidate keys with 'promote:pending' and a TTL; an automatic cleanup job demotes candidates older than the TTL unless 'promote-confirm' was set. Added TTL config and docs.
Lina Zhou: Request change: tighten RBAC in the Helm chart; don't grant promoter SA cluster-admin. Also add unit tests for label canonicalization.
Clara Mendes: Addressed: promoter only gets namespaced secret access and specific KMS/Cloud HSM policy bindings. Added tests and updated chart.
ci_checks: integration-smoke: fail on first run (vault test flake), retried -> pass
release_notes: Added expiring-cert-promoter operator to pre-stage certificate/key promotions for private installs. Included Helm hooks and Terraform KMS labels to enable staged, rollback-safe certificate rotations with HSM compatibility. See docs/operations/promote-playbook.md for runbook and rollback steps.
manual_steps_for_ops: 1) Ensure Terraform KMS module 'promote_labels' is set for HSM providers. 2) Install chart with enablePromoter=true. 3) Run helm hook 'pre-promote' to dry-run. 4) Verify candidate cert in Vault and set 'promote-confirm' annotation when ready. 5) Post-promote job performs pointer swap; if failure, run rollback script in docs to restore pointers within grace period.
additional_notes: This PR intentionally avoids auto-destruct of old keys to preserve forensic capability and to support forced rollback. Coordinate with HSM admin for providers that require offline approvals.
